band_light_definition: Lighting: soft warm light from the direction the face is turned toward, entering low and wide from beyond the edge of the frame the sitter looks at, so it reaches the sitter as one gentle horizontal band at eye level. Nothing that makes the light is ever visible, and the light has no stripes and no hard edges anywhere; it is simply a band of soft light lying across the face and the wall at eye height, softer above and below. The whole face is lit; the light is simply fullest across the eyes, the bridge and tip of the nose, the cheekbones and the mouth, and it stays on the brow, the chin and the jaw. The light sits most evenly on the bridge and tip of the nose and the cheekbone beside it, so the outline of the nose against the wall reads cleanly; the nose itself is neither brightened nor reshaped by the light, with no bright spot on its tip or bridge. Only above the hairline does the light begin to ease: the top of the hair and the wall above the head go gradually into soft shade toward the top edge of the frame. Only below the jaw does it ease underneath: the neck, the shoulders, the chest, the clothing and the wall below go gradually into the same soft shade toward the bottom edge; even the darkest part of the frame still shows detail. The wall keeps its own hue throughout: at its true colour and brightest at eye level, a little darker toward the top and bottom edges only; on a pale wall this is just a slightly brighter zone at eye level with no edge to it, the upper and lower edges of the frame a shade deeper, the same paint with a little less light on it, not a different colour and not a muddy one. The shading runs only from top to bottom, a plain top-to-bottom gradient and nothing else, like light from a wide, low source beyond the frame that covers the whole width of the frame evenly. The sides of the frame are not darkened, and the wall may be a little brighter on the side the face is turned toward, as it is in any room lit from one side. The four corners are no darker than the edge beside them; the corners and the sides look exactly as they would without the band. The effect is restrained: a viewer feels a quiet light resting on the face first and notices the gentle shading at the top and bottom only afterwards.

rationale:
Yes, it is done. Corrected templates are assembled and checked at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-IEMS-490/76d8a8da-60ab-5cff-aaff-4a9af2d4536b/scratchpad/final_v2.json (script: build_v2.py in the same folder; it asserts band_light_definition occurs exactly once, byte-identical, in all four templates, and scans for the banned effect words). I re-read G1 and E4 before deciding the conflicting fixes.

What G1 actually shows (corrected reading): a profile facing frame-right, lit from the direction the face points. The brow, eye, nose, cheek, mouth and chin are all lit; only the crown and top of the hair ease up into shade, and the jacket eases down while keeping its texture. The wall in front of the face is a little brighter than the wall behind the head, as with any single side light; the vertical falloff is the signature, and the mild side gradient is kept. E4 shows how little mauve is wanted and how warm it is; because in E4 it sits in the skin shadow under the closed eye and along the cheek, the brand rule deliberately moves it off the face into hair, cloth and charcoal wall.

FIXES APPLIED
1. Critical, bandit-mask stripe: shade no longer begins at the forehead and chin. New wording: the whole face is lit, fullest across eyes, nose bridge and tip, cheekbones and mouth, staying on the brow, chin and jaw; shade begins only above the hairline and only below the jaw. Merged the two reviewers' versions (critical fix plus 'mouth in the band').
2. Sides sentence ('edges exactly as bright as the middle of the same row'): replaced with the G1-accurate version: shading runs only top to bottom, sides not darkened, wall may be a little brighter on the side the face is turned toward, corners no darker than the edge beside them. Chose this over the alternative 'wall at edges exactly as bright as wall beside the sitter' because G1 and originals 1, 5, 6, 7 have the mild side gradient and 'exactly' invites over-correction.
3. Negatives sentence ('no dark ring ... no spotlight circle'): deleted; replaced by the positive 'the corners and the sides look exactly as they would without the band'. Merged with the other reviewer's 'plain top-to-bottom gradient and nothing else'.
4. Nose sentence: replaced with 'light sits most evenly on the bridge and tip of the nose and the cheekbone beside it, so the outline of the nose against the wall reads cleanly; the nose itself is neither brightened nor reshaped by the light, with no bright spot on its tip or bridge'. Kept one neutral wording (not 'exactly as it is' vs 'ordinary nose') so the definition stays identical in the t2i template; the t2i realism block already carries 'a real, ordinary nose of natural size and shape for this person'.
5. Window/blind/slot/slats/bars: all removed from the definition (chose the high-severity 'drop the window entirely' over the medium 'roller blind' rewrite, since the Background line already says 'no window visible'). Light is now 'soft warm light from the direction the face is turned toward, entering low and wide from beyond the edge of the frame the sitter looks at', with 'nothing that makes the light is ever visible'. 'Slats' also dropped from the negation; only 'no stripes and no hard edges' remain. Hopeful variant no longer raises a blind: 'more of the same light reaches the sitter and the band of light is taller'.
6. 'Beam' and 'strip' removed: 'like light from a wide, low source beyond the frame that covers the whole width of the frame evenly'; 'a slightly brighter zone at eye level with no edge to it'.
7. 'Daylight' became 'soft warm light' (originals, E3, E5 and Portra all lean warm); 'overcast morning' removed.
8. 'Never grey, brown or dirty' became 'not a different colour and not a muddy one' so the definition no longer forbids grey, brown or charcoal walls their own colour.
9. 'Does not notice the shading' became 'notices the gentle shading at the top and bottom only afterwards' so standard and hopeful cannot both collapse to flat.
10. Standard 'How much': now wall-to-wall (same wall at eye level vs top/bottom edges), compared to 'a wall a few steps further from the light', 'only seen when looking for it'; edit templates add 'no part of the frame is darker than the darkest part of the reference photograph'. Phrased as 'further from the light' rather than 'from a window' to keep the window out.
11. Hopeful 'How much': deleted 'nothing goes fully black or even deep grey' and 'the whole picture is as bright as'. Now: face lit as indoors on a mild, bright afternoon with the sun behind thin cloud, in the same warm colour; edges only a touch less lit, visible only side by side with a more shaded picture; the light reaches higher and lower (hairline and collar lit as fully as the cheek) as the visible lever that does not touch skin; charcoal stays charcoal and black hair stays black with texture visible; 'the shade opens up, not the skin'; 'expression, gaze and pose exactly the reference's; only the light is more open' (no 'smile', no 'hope' on the face). Dropped the near-zero 'cheek vs bridge' comparison.
12. Opening line (edit templates): 'colour grade of the picture, not the colours of the person' plus 'the new light changes only how bright each part of the sitter is; it does not change the shape or size of anything, and every shadow on the face falls where it falls in the reference'. Purple template says 'colour grade of the deepest tones'.
13. Purple paragraph: leads with 'In the deepest tones only' (no 'split-tone'); the four-colour-word face list next to 'under the eyes' and 'the nose' is gone, replaced by 'The skin carries none of it: face, neck and hands stay their own true colour in shadow as well as in light, warm and neutral, and the lit band across the face stays clean'; mauve on the wall restricted to 'a charcoal wall only', 'any other wall colour carries none of it' (slate navy would go violet, forest green would go mud).
14. t2i: 'in an easy natural profile turned a little toward the camera ... head at ease, shoulders soft' for batch consistency; 'never a clinical profile photograph' deleted; 'bare ears and neck, hands out of frame, wearing nothing on the face' replaces the negated jewellery/glasses list; colour block anchored to the {PERSON} description: 'the skin is exactly the depth and tone named for this person, rendered at that depth and no lighter'. TEMPLATE NOTE for {PERSON}: it must always state, in plain words, gender presentation, age range, ancestry, skin tone by depth (e.g. 'deep brown skin', 'medium olive skin', 'pale skin'), and hair colour, texture and length; without that the 'no lighter' clause has nothing to hold to and the model defaults pale.
15. Rationale misreadings of G1 and E4 corrected (above).

FIXES REJECTED OR MERGED RATHER THAN TAKEN LITERALLY
- 'Wall at the left and right edges exactly as bright as the wall right beside the sitter': rejected in favour of the mild side gradient, because it contradicts G1 and the originals.
- 'Roller blind' rewrite of the first sentence: rejected, because it still names a window and a blind twice in a prompt whose Background line already says 'no window visible'.
- 'Like light from a wide, low window crossing the frame' and 'a face beside a large window': not used verbatim, for the same reason; the level anchor is 'lit indoors on a mild, bright afternoon with the sun behind thin cloud'.
- 'Shaded side of a face ... lit by a large soft window, not a lamp' comparison: superseded by the wall-to-wall comparison, which is the one that is true on pearl white and peach.
- 'By about as much as the side of the nose is darker than its bridge' for hopeful: not used, because it puts a shadow comparison on the nose in a rhinoplasty prompt and the side-by-side sentence already sets the dose.
- 'Nose ... exactly as it is' in the definition with a different sentence in t2i: rejected because the definition must be byte-identical across the four; the neutral wording covers both.
- Standard and hopeful colour blocks keep the verified 'no purple, mauve or magenta anywhere on the face': kept as-is because it was in the verified template, uses no under-eye or nose region words, and no reviewer flagged it there.
- 'No jewellery' in t2i: not restored; 'bare ears and neck' covers it positively.

Usage note: pair the hopeful variant with the pale walls first (pearl white, peach, dusty rose, light cool grey), since that is where 'a little less dark' is most visible without touching the skin; run people_band on three references first (one pearl white, one charcoal, one deep skin tone). If the sides still darken, strengthen the 'sides of the frame are not darkened' sentence, not the dose; if a stripe appears, move 'no stripes and no hard edges' to the very end of the definition as well.
